**Status: Referred to a claims handler**

The claims subagent could not read the contract during its run, so I checked the contract myself and confirmed its findings against Articles 2, 3, 4 and 7. The claim was opened in the system and escalated to a human handler. Nothing was approved or refused.

**Facts recorded**
- Claim reference: trial-CLM-C. Policy VER-1003, holder Ines Haddad.
- Vehicle: Toyota Yaris (2019), market value EUR 9,000, per the Policy Schedule.
- Coverage claimed: C4 Theft, which is listed in the Policy Schedule.
- Incident date: 15 October 2026. Reported: 19 October 2026 (email date), 4 days later.
- The car was stolen from the street outside the customer's home. She was travelling and has not yet reported the theft to the police.
- No repair cost is stated. No documents are attached. No third party is involved.

**Reasoning**
- **Coverage:** C4 Theft is in the Policy Schedule, so the claim is under a covered coverage. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/> (Article 2 applies only to coverages listed in the Policy Schedule, and the Schedule lists C4.)
- **Late report:** A theft must be reported within 2 days of its discovery. The email does not state exactly when the theft was discovered. If it was discovered on 15 October, the report on 19 October is late. A late claim is referred to a claims handler and is never refused automatically. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/> <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="3" name="contract.pdf"/> (Articles 4.1 and 7.1.)
- **Missing document:** For C4 Theft, a police report is required. The customer has not yet made one. A missing document is not a refusal: it is requested from the policyholder. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/> (Article 4.3.)
- **Possible exclusion:** None is indicated by the story or the system checks. The Article 3 exclusions (alcohol, licence, racing, intentional damage, wear) are not mentioned in the email. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/> (Article 3.)
- **Settlement:** Not computed. The claim is referred for a human decision.

**Amounts:** Not computed. For the handler's reference only: the contract's theft amount is the market value of the vehicle, and the standard theft deductible is 10% of the claim, with a minimum of €500. The actual figures must come from the settlement tool once the handler decides. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>

**Draft message to the customer**

> Dear Ms Haddad,
>
> Thank you for reporting the theft of your Toyota Yaris on 15 October 2026. We have opened your claim (reference trial-CLM-C) and passed it to a Veridia claims handler, who will review it. Because your report reached us four days after the incident, the handler will look at the timing as part of the review. Please send us a police report or crime reference number for the theft as soon as you can. We will be in touch once the handler has made a decision.
>
> Kind regards,
> Veridia Claims
